out.rationale: Bowman et al. define scalable oversight as reliable supervision that remains effective past broadly human-level performance. Sudhir et al. cite Bowman et al. and describe it as a feedback mechanism that scales to superhuman intelligence, framing it either as a training method making honesty the best policy or as an inference-time mechanism-design problem.
out.scope: proposed DEPENDS_ON: the definition of scalable oversight cited by Sudhir et al.

text: The authors describe scalable oversight (citing Bowman et al. 2022) as the problem of developing a human feedback mechanism that scales to superhuman intelligences, and give two framings: a training method that makes honesty (or alignment) the best policy for the model, extending RLHF to the superhuman realm, or an inference-time mechanism that catches a model when it says something false or does something bad, framed as mechanism design.
title: Scalable oversight as a training method or as an inference-time oversight mechanism
